title: The Truth of Ten Thousand Years Ago
next_chapter_hook: The emissary's profound gaze locked onto Chen Ji, awaiting his choice—would he become the blade that resists Cang Yutian, or continue to be a chess piece manipulated at will in this ancient game spanning countless ages?

text.content: The Tianji Record's trembling was like a thunderclap exploding within the depths of Chen Ji's divine consciousness. The temptation of that forbidden secret technique seemed torn open by an invisible hand, revealing the unfathomable darkness beneath. His fingertips hovered mid-air, cold sweat winding down his spine. Never before had the Tianji Record warned him so intensely—unless the price about to be paid was sufficient to annihilate everything he had painstakingly built. The candlelight in the hall wavered, stretching the emissary's shadow like a specter, those scrutinizing eyes seeming to have already pierced through all his disguises.

The imperial emissary stepped forward slowly, the dark golden patterns on his black robe flowing like living things beneath the candlelight, each pattern seemingly recording unspeakable secrets. His voice was not loud, yet it clearly pierced through the silence, carrying a压制一切的威势：Chen Ji, do you know how Cang Yutian achieved the position of Heavenly Dao? What bloody原始积累 lies hidden behind those legendary feats? The corner of the emissary's mouth lifted in a meaningful smile, and the temperature in the hall seemed to drop several degrees.

dialogue.content: Twelve thousand years ago, before Cang Yutian achieved enlightenment, he was merely an ordinary cultivator with moderate talent. It was seven followers who accompanied him through life and death who dedicated their entire lives' effort to help him attain the Heavenly Dao.

text.content: Chen Ji's heart tightened. The Tianji Record fragments occasionally mentioned ancient mysteries, but never a single word about this. His gaze swept the four corners of the hall without a trace of emotion, confirming there were no other ambushes before speaking, his voice steady to the point of coldness: 'And then?' Since the emissary knows of this past, surely he knows what followed. The emissary's smile deepened, that smile carrying the vicissitudes and hatred of ten thousand years.

dialogue.content: 'The sequel? The sequel is the birth of the Heavenly Dao, yet the Chess Player was sealed away. Cang Yutian's first decree upon ascending to the Heavenly Dao position was to cast those seven followers into eternal imprisonment—because he feared, feared that those who knew his past would threaten his supreme authority.'

text.content: Silence like death filled the hall. Chen Ji felt the Tianji Record trembling slightly in his consciousness, not a warning, but an eerie resonance. He suddenly remembered what Mo Xiansheng had said—that every holder of the Tianji Record is a chosen chess piece. At the time, he dismissed it as the ravings of a remnant soul, but now it struck him like thunder. Mo Xiansheng, Cang Yutian, the seven followers... these threads intertwined frantically in his mind, weaving a net that made his spine chill.

dialogue.content: Among those seven, one fortunately escaped the sealing. Through ten thousand years, he transformed into the shadow of the Heavenly Will, accumulating strength in the darkness, only to wait for an opportunity—to overthrow Cang Yutian and reclaim the Heavenly Dao position that should have been theirs.

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. The shadow of Heavenly Will? A thought flashed through his mind like lightning—the Eye of Heavenly Secrets. That terrifying existence that ran through the entire book, viewing him as a chess piece. The final antagonist he would only become aware of in Volume Eight. Ten thousand years of lurking, all for revenge... He suddenly understood why the Tianji Record trembled so intensely. It sensed its own kind, sensed the ten-thousand-year burning obsession of one who had been betrayed.

choice.prompt: The imperial emissary's words shifted, throwing out a fatal question.

choices.description: Pressing for more details about the escaped one, and the true intentions of the remnant forces of the old Heavenly Dao. As a Chess Player, one cannot tolerate information asymmetry.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing more trump cards to unknown forces
choices.visible_reward: Obtaining crucial intelligence to formulate targeted strategies
choices.risk_hint: The other party might use this to probe the secrets of the Tianji Record

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes flickered slightly, suppressing the great waves within his heart. He slowly drew back his hovering fingertips, straightened his robe, and raised his eyes to stare directly at the emissary: 'Since you are willing to speak frankly, I would like to ask—where is the one who escaped the sealing now?' His voice was unhurried, revealing a composure that suggested understanding everything. The candlelight in the hall reflected on his calm features, showing no trace of panic.

choices.description: Not blindly trusting one-sided words, demanding the emissary prove the truth of what he said. Before solid evidence, any information could be a trap.
choices.visible_cost: Possibly missing the opportunity to obtain intelligence
choices.visible_reward: Avoiding being exploited by enemy forces, maintaining strategic initiative
choices.risk_hint: The emissary might lose patience as a result

text.content: Chen Ji stepped back, creating distance between himself and that forbidden secret technique. A cold smile appeared at the corner of his lips: 'What you just said is truly shocking. Heavenly secrets from ten thousand years ago, Cang Yutian betraying his followers... anyone could fabricate such words.' He raised his hand, the faint glow of the Tianji Record flowing in his palm: 'If you truly represent the remnants of the old Heavenly Dao, you should have some token to prove your identity.'

choices.description: Make no promises, observe this battle between gods and demons from a bystander's stance. Whichever side prevails has nothing to do with him—at least, that's how it appears on the surface.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain strategic space for remaining uninvolved
choices.risk_hint: Miss the opportunity to understand the truth

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his eyelids, concealing the turbulent thoughts churning in his gaze. His tone was cold to the point of alienation: What you speak of, Chen has heard and stored in his heart. As for believing or not believing... that's another matter entirely. He turned, his back facing the envoy: The three great sects clash, the Demonic Path invades, the Forbidden Grounds open—Chen is merely a worthless disciple struggling just to survive. How could he possibly possess the virtue to participate in a battle at the Heavenly Dao level?

Upon hearing this, the envoy did not become angry; instead, he let out a low chuckle. That laughter echoed through the spacious hall, carrying the weight of ten thousand years along with a sense of release. Chen Ji, do you truly believe this is a game you can remain outside of? He approached slowly, the dark gold patterns on his black robe suddenly lighting up, sketching a faint pattern in the void—a torn scroll, remarkably similar to the outline of the Tianji Record.

dialogue.content: The Tianji Record was not Cang Yutian's creation, but rather a relic of the one who escaped. Its selection of you is merely one piece in the ten-thousand-year layout of the remnants of the old Heavenly Dao. Your so-called 'foresight of the future' is merely the means by which that escaped one peers into the present world through the Tianji Record.

text.content: Chen Ji's breath stopped at this moment. Countless fragments in his mind suddenly clicked into place—why does Mo Xiansheng exist as a remnant soul on the first page of the Tianji Record? Why does the Tianji Record consume Heavenly Fate Value with each use? Are those vague foresight visions truly his own ability? He felt a bone-deep chill, as if the frost condensed from ten thousand years was climbing up his spine. The chess game he had meticulously woven, everything he thought he controlled, was merely a single piece on a much larger board.

dialogue.content: Of course, you may also choose not to believe.

text.content: The envoy raised his hand, and the candles in the hall extinguished at once. In the darkness, his figure became even clearer, his eyes like two balls of cold ghostly fire, gazing at Chen Ji without a trace of emotion: But there is one thing you must understand—whether you believe or not, Cang Yutian has already noticed you. The spiritual fluctuation of the Tianji Record was sensed by the Heavenly Dao three days ago when the Forbidden Grounds opened. Do you truly believe those 'coincidental' protections are merely coincidences?

Chen Ji's heart sank completely. When the Forbidden Grounds opened three days ago, he used the Tianji Record to peer into the future and indeed felt a faint sense of being watched. At that time, he merely thought it was the formation reaction of the Forbidden Grounds themselves, but now... his fingertips trembled slightly, an emotional fluctuation he was desperately trying to conceal. The obsession of ten thousand years ago, the covetousness of ten thousand years later, Cang Yutian's gaze—he was trapped between three forces, and he didn't even know who the real enemy was.

choice.prompt: The envoy extended a hand, and an ancient token hovered above his palm, inscribed with the two characters 'Tianji'.

choices.description: Temporarily accept the recruitment by the remnants of the old Heavenly Dao to buy himself breathing room. The enemy of one's enemy may not be a friend, but at least they can be utilized.
choices.visible_cost: May be exploited by the remnants of the old Heavenly Dao
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the protection of a faction
choices.risk_hint: Become a piece in a larger chess game

dialogue.content: Chen Ji was silent for a moment before finally reaching out and accepting the token. The moment the token touched his palm, a cold aura spread from his palm throughout his entire body, as if something was trying to invade his soul. His expression unchanged, he stored the token in his sleeve: I'll keep it for now. But Chen has one condition—no matter what schemes you harbor, my sister Chen Nian is not part of this deal.

choices.description: Not accept the token, but don't completely burn bridges either. Probe the other party's bottom line through words to obtain more intelligence about the organizational structure of the old Heavenly Dao remnants.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain independence and fight for the initiative in negotiations
choices.risk_hint: The envoy may not give a second chance

text.content: Chen Ji did not reach out, merely letting his gaze fall upon the token, a trace of mockery flickering in his eyes: Your kindness, Chen gratefully acknowledges. But Chen has one flaw—he dislikes owing favors and dislikes receiving things of unclear origin. He shifted topics: Among those seven followers, only one escaped with their life? The other six... is there any possibility of revival?

The envoy's smile slightly froze, as if not expecting him to counter-question at this moment. Chen Ji caught this momentary change and secretly noted it—the question had touched the enemy's vital point. He lowered his eyelids, retreating to advance: Since you mention a ten-thousand-year layout, surely you won't mind Chen learning more. After all... he raised his eyes, his gaze like a blade: If I'm to become one of your pieces, I must know how large this game truly is.

The atmosphere within the hall shifted subtly. The messenger studied him for a long while before finally speaking: Six companions have all perished, their remnant souls scattered far and wide. However, one person's legacy has not been severed—Mo Xiansheng... no, he should be called Mo Yuan. He was once the most skilled strategist among the seven, and after death, he entrusted his remnant soul to the Tianji Record, awaiting a suitable host to appear. Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Mo Xiansheng. The Remnant Soul Guardian. That mysterious existence who knew all the truths of the Tianji Record yet only revealed what should be said. All his schemes, it turned out, had been manipulated from the start by an invisible hand.

dialogue.content: Do you understand now? Mo Yuan chose you to use your hands to break the seal and rescue the Lord eternally imprisoned within the Heavenly Dao prison. Cang Yutian's position on the Heavenly Dao was built upon betrayal and lies. The old Heavenly Dao's revival will tear off his hypocritical mask.

text.content: Chen Ji felt an unprecedented absurdity. He laughed bitterly, that smile carrying self-mockery and desolation: He had thought he was the chess player, calculating every move without flaw, advancing methodically. Yet from beginning to end, he was merely a piece on someone else's chessboard. Mo Xiansheng chose him to be used; Cang Yutian allowed his growth to use him as a piece; and now the old Heavenly Dao remnants seek him out, equally to drag him into the chess game. He, Chen Ji, had lived over twenty years without ever truly playing a single move for himself.

choice.prompt: The messenger gently placed the token on the table and stepped back.

choices.description: Since all are pieces, then overturn the board. The Tianji Record is his—he will control his own destiny, even if it means making enemies of Heaven.
choices.visible_cost: Make an enemy of Cang Yutian, lose Tianqing Sect's protection
choices.visible_reward: Completely control the Tianji Record, embark on an independent path
choices.risk_hint: May simultaneously offend two major powers

dialogue.content: Chen Ji suddenly laughed, that laughter echoing through the empty hall, carrying a近乎疯狂的洒脱. He raised his hand, and the Tianji Record's brilliant light bloomed in his palm: Since we're all pieces, then I will no longer be a piece. Cang Yutian wants to destroy me, the old Heavenly Dao wants to use me, Mo Xiansheng treated me as a tool from the start—fine, today I, Chen Ji, will carve a bloody path through this crevice!

choices.description: Temporarily feign compliance, use the old Heavenly Dao remnants' resources against Cang Yutian. After weakening both sides, reap the fisherman's profit.
choices.visible_cost: May fall deep into the old Heavenly Dao's conspiracy
choices.risk_hint: May be completely controlled by the old Heavenly Dao

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's smile faded, replaced by a deep calculation. He picked up the token on the table, examining it carefully: What you say is correct. Since we are all pieces, then let us see who can better exploit this piece's identity. He tucked the token into his sleeve: The Forbidden Grounds assembly in three days—I will attend. But how I act will be decided by myself.

text.content: A strange glint flickered in the messenger's gaze, seemingly quite satisfied with this answer. He微微点头: A wise person knows when to advance and retreat. You are different from those fools—Cang Yutian chose you as a candidate for the chess player for good reason. He turned, his robe sleeve brushing the dust in the hall, stirring cold points of light: At the Forbidden Grounds assembly in three days, the sealed Lord will attempt to speak with you. Then... you will understand everything.

As the words fell, the messenger's figure dissolved like ink scattered by wind, gradually fading from Chen Ji's sight. The hall returned to darkness, save for that scroll of forbidden secret art on the table still emitting a ghostly glow, as if silently mocking something. Chen Ji stood alone in the hall, the ice-cold token in his hand, his heart churning with indescribable emotions. The truth of ten thousand years ago, the old Heavenly Dao remnants' covetousness, Cang Yutian's covert observation—he had been drawn into the center of a storm far beyond imagination. And the promise he made to the messenger just now—was it a strategy to break the situation, or the beginning of another trap? The Tianji Record trembled slightly in the depths of his divine consciousness, as if also awaiting that approaching answer.
